page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-2 is an entry-level virtual machine belonging to the Compute Optimized family. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core with 2 threads. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It comes with 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. Local storage is not bundled, requiring external network-attached storage disks, and no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core tests at 2923.48 and achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 1620.0. In contrast, overall multi-core and throughput performance is severely capped by the 2-vCPU hardware footprint. Multi-core stress-ng (2928.18) and Geekbench multi-core (2021.0) land in the bottom percentiles, as do compilation tasks, ray tracing, and static web serving throughput (2.82 GB/sec). Memory bandwidth reaches 33.76 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 24.26 GB/sec for uncached write operations, which reflects low memory subsystem aggregate bandwidth.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the c2d-standard-2 provides a cost-effective route to access dedicated AMD EPYC performance without paying for large resource blocks. However, its small core count and lack of integrated NVMe storage make it unsuitable for high-concurrency database systems, heavy parallel data science pipelines, or high-volume web traffic. The instance is best matched for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight CI/CD build nodes, microservices, and general compute workloads with low parallel processing demands.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-2 is a compute-oriented virtual machine equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, driven by a single physical core of an AMD EPYC 7B13 x86_64 processor. The configuration features 32 MB of L3 cache, no bundled local storage, and zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluation reveals robust single-core compute performance, ranking in the upper 25% on stress-ng single-core suites. However, the limited core count yields modest multi-core scores, lower memory throughput (33.76 GB/sec uncached reads), and reduced concurrency in Redis operations (2.22 million ops/sec) and web serving. The c2d-standard-2 provides cost-efficient access to AMD EPYC compute power for low-overhead general purpose services, lightweight single-threaded tasks, microservices, and modest CI/CD pipeline steps.
